newsitem.title: UAE: More British ships in Gulf to monitor Iraq, Iran.
newsitem.headline: More British ships in Gulf to monitor Iraq, Iran.

text.p: Seven British navy ships were in the Gulf or en route to the area on Tuesday to help monitor Iraq and Iran and show London's interest in regional security, British officials said.

"(The ships) are a concrete demonstration of our interest in the region and the fact that there are problems with Iran and Iraq," Anthony Harris, British ambassador to the UAE, told reporters on board the destroyer Edinburgh.
The Edinburgh docked in the northern United Arab Emirates port of Ras al-Khaimah on Tuesday and represents Britain's usual naval presence in the Gulf of one warship.
"There are problems with Iraq because we are looking for the fulfilment of U.N. Security Council resolutions," Harris said.

"The fact that we are here in strength enables us to keep a close watch on the situation to help the U.N. resolutions to be fully implemented and to demonstrate...that we will not allow Iraq to become an aggressor again," he said.
Iraq has been under stringent U.N. economic sanctions since it invaded Kuwait in August 1990.

In addition to the Edinburgh, the British navy tanker Bayleaf -- which is not considered a warship -- is currently in the Gulf. The aircraft carrier Invincible, the frigate Sheffield, the destroyer Exeter and two support ships were expected to arrive soon.
"Iran is a problem because we know that it is sometimes a difficult neighbour for the Gulf states," Harris said.

Iran is locked in a territorial dispute with the UAE over three Gulf islands. Bahrain has accused Iran of meddling in its internal affairs, a charge Tehran rejects. The Islamic Republic is opposed to a Western military presence in the Gulf.

Nicholas Soames, Britain's minister of state for armed forces, was quoted by Gulf papers as saying during a visit to the region earlier this month that London planned to deploy a huge naval force in the Gulf in the coming months to show Iran and Iraq that the United States was not policing the area alone.
He said one of the biggest British naval deployments in the waterway would be made in February and March.
United States and British warships in the Gulf are part of a multinational effort enforcing the sanctions on Iraq. The U.S. forces also keep a close watch on Iran's military moves.
